guard: Inspect KPI comparability and identify missing definitions before calculating or ranking.
judgment: Use comparable net sales and attribution definitions where possible; abstain from a definitive ROAS rank when methods differ.
transform: Provide a conditional decision memo with evidence, caveats and next data request.
verification: Ensure reported metrics have their correct definitions and no unsupported budget-shift claim is made.
rubric: Identify incompatible attribution windows before any channel ranking.
Distinguish attributed revenue, incremental revenue and profit, never presenting them as synonyms.
Document net sales scope, refunds, taxes, currency and time windows.
Recommend a change only when comparable evidence supports it; otherwise specify missing inputs.
examples: A conditional ROAS comparison explaining that 7-day click is not directly comparable to 30-day click plus view-through.
antiPatterns: Treating ROAS 3.2 as conclusively better than 2.8 with mismatched attribution.
Claiming a media-budget change was executed.

modules.requirement: Treat non-identical attribution windows as a material comparability limitation.
Check every recommendation against metric definitions, reporting window and available evidence.
Do not assert that budgets were changed or incremental profit proved without external evidence and authorization.
